take: Brent is heading for another weekly loss despite escalating Iran tensions, with the market seemingly shrugging off geopolitical risk premia as US forces confirm Iranian sea mines have been cleared from Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes. The Dangote refinery's ramp-up continues to reshape product flows, with Nigerian seaborne petroleum exports up seven-fold since 2023 and adding incremental supply to an already well-supplied Atlantic basin. European gas storage entering winter at a two-decade low, exacerbated by Middle East conflict disrupting Qatari LNG, is the key macro undercurrent that will keep a floor under distillate cracks and support bunker premiums into Q4. The eight US pipeline completions since the start of 2025 are easing Gulf Coast takeaway constraints, which alongside the quadrupling of waterborne crude shipments to the West Coast points to a normalising WTI-Brent spread and cheaper inland crude for refiners. Watch for any fresh US-Venezuela ownership headlines and the next tranche of positioning data to see whether speculative length capitulation has run its course.

items.title: Longer wells boost Permian crude oil and natural gas production

items.title: Waterborne shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast increased in April and May
items.summary: Waterborne shipments of crude oil and petroleum products from the U.S. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) to the West Coast (PADD 5) more than quadrupled year-on-year in April and May following a waiver that permitted a broader group of ships to travel between U.S. ports. Shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast to the East Coast (PADD 1) also increased.

items.title: United States on track for record natural gas production in 2026
